relationships.description: The index is keyed on this field as one of its key or included members, grouping existing fields of the collection into a lookup structure without owning them, so the field persists if the index is dropped.
relationships.evidence: The index definition (e.g. a CREATE INDEX statement, MongoDB createIndex key document, DynamoDB GSI KeySchema, or search mapping) lists the field's name or path among its keyed or included fields.

relationships.description: The index lets the engine resolve this access pattern's key, sort or filter conditions by direct lookup or range scan instead of a full collection scan, making the request cheaper and faster.
relationships.evidence: The index's leading key fields match the access pattern's key condition (and sort fields where applicable), as shown by a data-model design table mapping the pattern to the index or by a query plan (EXPLAIN) showing the index used for that query.
